clue.text: Team with a pretentious air.

definitions.meaning: a sports team or eleven, one of two opposing sets of players
putting on airs and graces, haughty swagger

explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting on side' is a dated British idiom for behaving pretentiously.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a team of players, and haughty swagger as in 'putting on side'.

clue.text: Scrappy knowledge of direction being important.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south, a compass direction
to matter is to be important, so being important is mattering

explanation.surface: A remark that someone's patchy grasp of which way to go actually matters a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight, superficial acquaintance with a subject is a fragmentary, bitty knowledge of it.

clue.text: Prevent the common little chap from cleansing.

parts.note: to deter is to prevent or discourage
gent is a common, informal shortening of gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: Someone is stopping an ordinary small man from washing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word describes something with a cleaning, purifying action, like soap.

clue.text: It's so much more than upright -magnificence is its keynote!

definitions.text: It's so much more than upright -magnificence is its keynote!

parts.words: It's so much more than upright -magnificence is its keynote!
parts.note: an upright is a domestic piano, so its bigger concert-hall cousin is a superior instrument whose leading feature, keynote, is splendour in name and sound

explanation.surface: Praise for something that outclasses mere uprightness through sheer splendour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' looks like a moral quality, but it is the small vertical piano; 'keynote' adds a musical pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The large horizontal concert instrument is the grander alternative to an upright domestic keyboard.

clue.text: Aimless chatter is meant to be engaging!

indicators.note: aimless suggests letters wandering without direction, so the word chatter is rearranged

explanation.surface: Pointless gossip is supposed to be charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaging' looks like 'charming', but a ratchet's pawl engages the teeth of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed mechanism designed so that a catch meshes with its teeth, letting it turn one way only.

clue.text: Has lived through part of the Bible.

definitions.meaning: one ... years when one has lived for that many, as in 'she ... eighty summers'
the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone has survived a section of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To count one's years of age is a literary way of saying one has lived them; the fourth Old Testament book bears this title.

clue.text: Taking a stroll by the clock tower doesn't. sound a very dynamic way of life!

definitions.text: Taking a stroll by the clock tower doesn't. sound a very dynamic way of life!

parts.words: Taking a stroll by the clock tower doesn't. sound a very dynamic way of life!
parts.note: walking past a clock tower literally goes by the hours shown on its face, and the idiom for idling away the hours hardly suggests an energetic existence

explanation.surface: A gentle walk beside a clock tower is hardly a vigorous lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop after doesn't is the newspaper's print. The phrase means both walking past a clock and idly filling hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means occupying oneself idly to fill hours, which literally describes strolling past a clock.

clue.text: It's a heavy blow-shame!

parts.note: a bash is a heavy blow or thump

explanation.surface: A hard knock is a disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To shame someone is to make them embarrassed and disconcerted, a verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: The grain seen in pipes.

definitions.meaning: a cereal crop eaten as porridge or fed to horses
pastoral poets wrote of shepherds' pipes made of oaten straw, the oaten reed of Milton

explanation.surface: Cereal visible inside tubes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cereal is a familiar grain, and its straw made the rustic shepherd's pipe of pastoral poetry.

clue.text: Appropriate form for reporting an insinuation?

definitions.text: Appropriate form for reporting an insinuation?

parts.words: Appropriate form for reporting an insinuation?
parts.note: reported speech is the grammatical form used for relaying what someone said, and an insinuation is itself a roundabout, oblique utterance

explanation.surface: A question about the right grammar for passing on a sly hint.
explanation.walkthrough: The grammatical term for reported speech also describes speaking by hints rather than plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Reported speech is the grammatical term for relaying words, and an oblique hint is talk that avoids saying things outright.

clue.text: Don't stop the play in London.

definitions.meaning: an instruction to carry on performing, to keep acting

explanation.surface: A plea to keep a London performance going.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a suburb in west London; split two-and-three it is an instruction to keep acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the name urges performers to keep going; whole, it is a west London district.

clue.text: Former issues of ourselves in the long long ago?

definitions.meaning: back numbers of this very newspaper, the Times, are its past editions

explanation.surface: Old copies of our own paper from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ourselves' is the newspaper speaking: this clue ran in The Sunday Times, so its old issues are Times past.
explanation.definitionFit: Past editions of the Times newspaper, and a poetic phrase for bygone days.

clue.text: Foreign transport goes down sweetly.

parts.note: Turkish is one particular foreign nationality, standing in for foreign generally
transport in the sense of rapture is delight

explanation.surface: Overseas vehicles descend gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like vehicles but means rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: The gel-like confection dusted in sugar is a sweet that is easy to swallow.

clue.text: Masses sent out to arrange for the tax.

indicators.note: the words are put out of order and then arranged anew, signalling a rearrangement of masses sent

explanation.surface: Crowds dispatched to organise a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax assessment is the sum levied on someone, so the word can stand for the levy itself.

clue.text: Keep in the same office.

parts.note: voters who return an official to the post they already hold choose them once more

explanation.surface: Retain someone in the same workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' looks like a workplace but means a public post.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting an official back into the post they held keeps them there for another term.

clue.text: They stood as — to the land, Each one a lovely light (Coleridge).

definitions.text: They stood as — to the land, Each one a lovely light (Coleridge).

parts.words: They stood as — to the land, Each one a lovely light (Coleridge).
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, where the angelic figures on deck stand as beacons shown to the shore

explanation.surface: A line of Coleridge's poem with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing word comes from The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, where the seraph-band stand like beacons to the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Beacons or lights shown to communicate with the shore are exactly what the seraphs resemble in the poem.

clue.text: Meet a tour to engage in a petty love affair.

indicators.note: the words meet a tour are put to work together, engaged in a fresh arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Joining a sightseeing trip in order to start a little romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A French diminutive of love, it names a brief, trivial romance or flirtation.

clue.text: No bird goes by first-class return according to my list!

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: return means the abbreviation for first-class is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, and the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A bird travels back first-class, as noted on a register.
explanation.walkthrough: NOTITIA is a rare word for a register or list.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare Latin-derived word for a register, roll or catalogue of names.

clue.text: He encourages one to place a wager with some prominence.

parts.note: a means one, the indefinite article
a bet is a wager
a tor is a rocky hill or prominence, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone urges a person to bet on something lofty.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop, familiar from Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice who eggs someone on, especially to wrongdoing, is an encourager.

clue.text: Special hat,'standing by itself, of Irish origin.

indicators.note: special suggests the hat is specially remade, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: something standing by itself is alone, lone

explanation.surface: A distinctive hat, standing apart, comes from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' rearranges HAT into ATH. ATHLONE is a town in the Irish midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the River Shannon in the Irish midlands, so a place one may hail from in Ireland.

clue.text: Golden girl? That's fishy!

definitions.meaning: a girl's name from the Latin for golden
a genus of jellyfish, the moon jelly, a sea creature loosely called fishy

explanation.surface: A doubtful remark about a glamorous girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name for a girl comes from aureus, gold; it is also the genus of moon jellyfish, marine creatures.

clue.text: Right! Barry sets trap cunningly to catch food!

indicators.note: cunningly suggests craftiness, so the letters are craftily rearranged

explanation.surface: Barry lays a clever trap to snare something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastries filled with a red summer berry are an item of food.

clue.text: Foreign friend has to leave with another.

parts.note: ami is French for friend
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: An overseas companion must depart together with someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: AMI is French for friend; the whole answer is Spanish for friend, so 'another' foreign friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a friend is another foreign word for a companion, besides the French one.

clue.text: Cleopatra's attendant turned up in this garment.

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the name is read backwards, bottom to top

parts.note: Iras is one of Cleopatra's waiting women in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra

explanation.surface: Cleopatra's servant appeared wearing this item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like 'arrived' but reverses IRAS, read upwards in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A draped length of cloth worn by women in South Asia is an item of clothing.

clue.text: … but surely I meant to change everything about supplying food?

indicators.note: everything sits about, around, the rearranged letters

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: to change means the letters of I meant are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker insists their intention was to transform everything to do with feeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To change' rearranges I MEANT into IMENTA, which goes inside ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something nourishing, giving nutriment or sustenance.

clue.text: Time during which a gourmet reacts to what's set before him.

indicators.note: during which signals letters found within the run of words gourmet reacts

explanation.surface: The moment when a food-lover responds to the dish placed before him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' is the musical sense: rhythm or beat.
explanation.definitionFit: In music and verse, time in the sense of rhythmic pattern or measure is the beat of the line.

clue.text: Hailstorm erupting around the East gives an indication of constant temperature.

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation
erupting suggests a violent outburst that scatters the letters of hailstorm

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A violent storm breaking out in the east signals stable weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erupting' rearranges HAILSTORM into ISOTHRMAL, which goes around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A line on a weather map joining places of equal temperature marks where warmth stays the same.

clue.text: Qualified in experience.

definitions.meaning: fit, suitable or proper, an old adjective

explanation.surface: Someone is fit in terms of experience.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means fitting or proper; as a verb it means to undergo or encounter.
